title.en: Mukesh and the bangle makers of Firozabad

hook.en: Glass bangles shine in every Indian market. In Firozabad, the town that makes many of them, children work beside hot furnaces to produce them.

objectives.en: Describe the glass bangle industry of Firozabad
Explain the hazards children face there

narration.en: Glass bangles shine in every Indian market. In Firozabad, the town that makes many of them, children work beside hot furnaces to produce them.

body.en: Firozabad is famous for its glass bangles, and almost every family there is engaged in making them. Many children work in dark, airless rooms near furnaces at very high temperatures, and the work damages their eyes; many adults go blind. Child labour in such hazardous work is illegal, yet it continues.

points.en: Town of glass bangles; families have worked at it for generations
Children work near hot furnaces in dingy cells
Child labour here is against the law but goes on

explanation.en: Child labour in such hazardous work is illegal, yet it goes on.

body.en: Mukesh belongs to a family of bangle makers. His father has worked hard all his life but could neither renovate the house nor send his sons to school. Mukesh is different: he wants to be a motor mechanic and drive a car, even if he has to walk a long way to the garage to learn. A young girl, Savita, solders pieces of glass, unaware of what bangles will mean to her one day as a bride.

points.en: Father: lifelong work, no savings, no schooling for sons
Mukesh: wants to be a motor mechanic
Savita: a young girl soldering glass

problem.en: What are the hazards of working in the glass bangle industry?

steps.en: Mention the working conditions: dingy cells near hot furnaces.
Mention the health damage: children and adults lose their eyesight.
Add that the work is illegal for children yet continues.

answer.en: Workers, including children, sit in dark, airless rooms beside furnaces at very high temperatures. The heat and the fine glass work damage their eyes, and many go blind. Though child labour here is illegal, it continues.
